name: PA-15
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans about nineteen points Republican, anchoring the race to the incumbent's advantage
Glenn Thompson holds a roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge over Ray Bilger with minimal outside spending on either side
Prediction markets price Thompson's reelection near ninety-five percent
No public polling or expert ratings signal a competitive race
model.rationale: The district's nineteen-point Republican lean, Thompson's incumbency and ten-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing the race near ninety-five percent Republican all point the same way, and no polling or outside spending suggests a contest. Even a favorable national environment for Democrats leaves this seat well out of range.
model.watch: A historic national wave or an unexpected development involving the incumbent could narrow the margin, though the structural advantage is unlikely to be overcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
PA-15 is a heavily Republican district in north-central Pennsylvania with a partisan lean of roughly nineteen points toward the GOP. Glenn Thompson has held the seat since 2009 and is running again after winning renomination. Democratic nominee Ray Bilger has raised about a tenth of Thompson's total and has drawn little outside support.

No public general-election polling covers the race, and outside groups have spent almost nothing on either side. Prediction markets give Thompson roughly a ninety-five percent chance of returning to office. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and a large financial edge — all align in the same direction, and even a strong national environment for Democrats would need to be extraordinary to put this seat in play. The race is rated Safe Republican.
